verdict.rationale: Clerk documents custom Roles and 'fine-grained Permissions' scoped to Organizations, which goes beyond the default admin/member roles. It also lets you gate eve tool calls against the caller's permissions and scopes. However, the evidence shows only org-scoped role/permission assignment, not resource-level relationship-based (ReBAC) or policy-based (ABAC) authorization. A community report notes that roles are tied to organizations, which supports reading this as RBAC rather than a resource-level model. Missing for 10: per-resource authorization (permissions on individual objects), a relationship-based model, a policy language or engine, and independent corroboration of fine-grained depth.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can express fine-grained, resource-level authorization (relationship- or policy-based) beyond simple roles

citations.quote: You can also create custom Roles and fine-grained Permissions that fit your application's specific features and team setup.
Gate individual eve tool calls against the caller's Clerk permissions and scopes
Organizations let you group users with Roles and Permissions.
